title: Independent Film
objective: After this level you can explain what makes a film independent and how low budgets can push filmmakers toward new ideas.
summary: Independent films are made outside the major studios. Cassavetes's Shadows and Romero's Night of the Living Dead found new ways on little money; Sundance gave independents a stage.

cards.headline: An early American independent film was paid for partly by radio listeners.
cards.body: John Cassavetes financed his first film as director, Shadows, partly with donations sent after he appealed for money on a radio program. No studio, no studio money. What makes a film independent, and what can a tiny budget push a filmmaker to try?

cards.headline: Outside the studio system
cards.body: Independent film simply means films produced outside the major studio system. Shadows shows what that looked like: shot on 16-mm film over about two and a half years, and semi-improvised. It is generally acknowledged to have started the American independent movement. Cassavetes paid for later films with his acting, which was wanted by the same studios that were reluctant to back his directing.

cards.headline: Friends, pooled money, new monsters
cards.body: In 1968 George Romero and several friends pooled their money to make Night of the Living Dead. Major studios rejected it; it became a cult favorite anyway. It also set the pattern for modern zombie movies by separating the monsters from Vodou and putting them in contemporary settings. A small budget didn't stop a new idea from taking over a genre.

cards.headline: A stage for independents
cards.body: Independents still needed an audience. The Sundance Film Festival began in 1978 in Salt Lake City as the Utah/United States Film Festival. It came under Robert Redford's Sundance Institute, founded to nurture independent filmmakers, and took the Sundance name in 1991. It became known for jump-starting careers, including those of the Coen brothers, Steven Soderbergh and Quentin Tarantino.

options.label: It was shot on 16-mm film
options.rationale: Shadows was, but the format isn't the definition.

options.label: It won a prize at Sundance
options.rationale: Sundance showcases independents; it doesn't define them.

options.label: It was produced outside the major studio system
Its dialogue was improvised
options.rationale: Improvising is a choice, not the definition.

questions.explanation: Independent film refers to films produced outside the major film studio system.

questions.prompt: Which example from this level best supports the idea that a low budget can push filmmakers toward new ideas?

options.label: Night of the Living Dead: pooled money, and a new pattern for zombie films
Sundance was renamed in 1991
options.rationale: A name change isn't a new filmmaking idea.

options.label: Major studios quickly bought Night of the Living Dead
Cassavetes acted in studio films
options.rationale: That funded his films; it wasn't the new idea.

questions.explanation: Romero's low-budget film, rejected by studios, reshaped the zombie movie with contemporary settings.

questions.prompt: Shadows and Breathless both made do with little money. What did Level 62 say Breathless did when it couldn't afford tracks?

options.label: Skipped the shot and used a still photo
options.rationale: The shot was made another way.

options.label: Borrowed tracks from a studio
options.rationale: They had none, so they improvised.

options.label: Pushed cinematographer Raoul Coutard along in a wheelchair

questions.explanation: Coutard shot handheld and was pushed in a wheelchair because the production couldn't afford tracks.
